subtitle: Midterm Important MCQs
topics: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
Gray Box and White Box Testing

mcqs.question: According to the professional view of quality, any deviation from the clearly stated requirements is regarded as a:
options: Feature
Defect
Enhancement
Failure

mcqs.question: According to the professional view, quality means:
options: Something good but not quantifiable
Something luxury and classy
Conformance to requirements and fitness for use
Maximum features at any cost

mcqs.question: The ISO 8402 definition of quality is:
options: The degree to which a system meets specified requirements
The totality of features and characteristics of a product or service that bear on its ability to satisfy stated or implied needs
Conformance to schedule and budget
The absence of defects in the delivered product

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six quality characteristics of the ISO 9126 model?
options: Functionality
Reliability
Maintainability
Testability

mcqs.question: "Quality is Zero Defects" is one of the:
options: ISO 9126 quality characteristics
Four Absolutes of quality
IEEE definitions of software quality
Objectives of SQA

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a benefit of software quality?
options: Increased rework
More defects and errors
Reduced development and maintenance cost
Lower customer satisfaction

mcqs.question: According to the IEEE definition, software quality is the degree to which a system, component, or process meets:
options: Only the budgetary requirements
Only the developer's expectations
Specified requirements, and customer or user needs or expectations
Only the implied needs of users

mcqs.question: From the customer's perspective, software quality is mainly concerned with:
options: Cost and schedule
Detection and correction times
Complete requirements (functional and non-functional)
Infrastructure and tools

mcqs.question: Software Quality Assurance provides adequate confidence that the software process conforms to:
options: Only the functional technical requirements
Established functional technical requirements as well as managerial requirements of keeping the schedule and operating within the budget
Only the customer's implied needs
Only the documentation standards

mcqs.question: Which unique characteristic of software means that missing parts of the product are not obvious and defects may not be noticeable for years?
options: High complexity
Invisibility of the product
Required teamwork
Being contracted

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: Quality Assurance is:
options: Product oriented and focuses on defect identification
Process oriented and focuses on defect prevention
A reactive quality process
Concerned only with the finished product

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: Quality Control is a set of activities for ensuring quality in products, and its activities focus on:
options: Preventing defects in the development process
Improving the test process
Identifying defects in the actual products produced
Periodic conformance audits of the system

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: Quality Assurance is a proactive process, whereas Quality Control is a:
options: Proactive process
Preventive process
Reactive process
Static process

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: The goal of Quality Assurance is to:
options: Identify defects after the product is developed and before it is released
Improve development and test processes so that defects do not arise when the product is being developed
Fix the bugs reported by customers
Certify that testing is complete

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: During the requirements phase, the SQA activity includes:
options: Verifying that all bugs in the bug tracking system are resolved
Ensuring that the user/client requirements are captured correctly and finding out the risks in the requirements
Verifying that all design documents are kept in the project repository
Compiling the test reports

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: Verification is best described by the question:
options: "Are we building the right product?"
"Are we building the product right?"
"Is the product completely free of defects?"
"Does the user accept the product?"

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: Validation checks that:
options: The software conforms to its specification
The documents follow the organizational standards
The software does what the user really requires
The code compiles without errors

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: Code and document inspections, which analyse the static representation of the system to discover problems, are an example of:
options: Dynamic verification and validation
Static verification and validation
Acceptance testing
Regression testing

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: In dynamic verification and validation (software testing):
options: Documents are reviewed by peers without executing the system
The system is executed with test data and its operational behaviour is observed
Only the source code structure is analysed
The specification is checked against standards

mcqs.topic: SQA in SDLC, Verification and Validation
mcqs.question: During the testing phase, SQA certifies that:
options: All captured requirements are allocated to software components
The verification matrix is updated regularly
Testing is complete according to the plan
The components are ready to start testing

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: In the error-defect-failure chain, an error is:
options: A human mistake
An improper program condition
A difference from the intended behaviour
A defect found during inspection

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: A failure is:
options: A human mistake made by the developer
An improper program condition resulting from an error
The difference between the actual behaviour and the intended behaviour of the system
A defect removed during inspection

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: An inspection is:
options: The execution of software with test data to observe its behaviour
A rigorous team review of a work product by peers of the producer of the work product
An audit performed by top management
An automated analysis of the source code

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: Software Quality Management (SQM) comprises which three processes?
options: Quality planning, testing and deployment
Verification, validation and reviews
Quality planning, quality assurance and quality control
Standards, audits and metrics

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: The starting point for the quality planning process is:
options: The project schedule
The standards followed by the organization
The test plan
The customer's contract

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: A quality plan sets out:
options: Only the project budget and schedule
Only the testing tools to be used
The desired product qualities, how these are assessed, and the most significant quality attributes
Only the development methodology

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: Product standards define:
options: How the software process should be enacted
Characteristics that all components should exhibit, e.g. a common programming style
The quality goals of the project
How defects are reported and tracked

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a problem associated with standards?
options: They encapsulate best practice
They provide continuity for new staff
They involve too much bureaucratic form filling
They provide a framework for the quality assurance process

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: Quality reviews are:
options: An automated software assessment technique
The principal method of validating the quality of a process or of a product
A form of dynamic testing
Performed only by the SQA group

mcqs.topic: Quality Management, Principles, Practices and Standards
mcqs.question: Defects per function point or defects per KLOC are examples of:
options: SQA principles
Quality plan inputs
Normalized defect data used in defect quality measurement
Inspection roles

mcqs.question: "Testing is the process of executing a program or system with the intent of finding errors." This definition of testing was given by:
options: Hetzel (1973)
Myers (1979)
Popper (1965)
Hetzel (1983)

mcqs.question: According to Myers, a test is said to be successful if it:
options: Proves that the program has no errors
Discovers an error
Executes all the statements of the program
Passes all the test cases

mcqs.question: The objective of testing is to:
options: Show the absence of defects in the software
Show the presence of a defect, not the absence of it
Prove the correctness of the program formally
Execute the program at least once

mcqs.question: Exhaustive testing of software is not possible because:
options: Testers do not have the required skills
Testing tools are not available
It is too expansive and needs virtually infinite resources
Programs are too small to test

mcqs.question: In the SDLC versus STLC comparison, development is a creative activity while testing is a:
options: Support activity
Destructive activity
Managerial activity
Documentation activity

mcqs.question: Which document is the starting point and base document for both testing and development?
options: Test plan
Bug report
Functional specification document
Design document

mcqs.question: After the development team fixes a defect and sends the patch, the testing team:
options: Closes the defect immediately
Runs the same test case/scenario again and closes the defect only if the problem does not appear again
Writes a new functional specification
Stops the testing process

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a category of testing techniques?
options: Requirement based testing
Schedule based testing
Specification based (black box) testing
Budget based testing

mcqs.question: Black box testing ignores:
options: The outputs generated by the system
The internal mechanism of a system or component
The specified functional requirements
The execution conditions

mcqs.question: Black box testing is also known as:
options: Structural testing
Glass box testing
Specification based testing
Code based testing

mcqs.question: In black box testing, test cases can be designed:
options: Only after the coding is complete
As soon as the functional specifications are complete
Only after unit testing is done
Only during the acceptance phase

mcqs.question: The aim of Equivalence Partitioning is to:
options: Test every possible input value
Treat groups of inputs as equivalent and select one representative input to test them all
Test only the boundary values of inputs
Test all the state transitions of the system

mcqs.question: For the condition "VALUE is between 1 and 100 (inclusive)", which of the following is a boundary value?
Boundary Value Analysis operates on the basis that:
options: Errors occur randomly in the input domain
Errors are most likely to exist at the boundaries between partitions
All inputs in a partition behave differently
Exhaustive testing is possible at boundaries

mcqs.question: Decision table testing is especially useful for:
options: Measuring code coverage
Testing simple input ranges
Complex business rules where different combinations of inputs result in different actions
Testing the format of input data

mcqs.question: State transition testing is used for:
options: Batch processing systems
Real time systems with various states and transitions involved
Database query testing
Compiler testing

mcqs.question: In use case testing, the test cases based on use cases are referred to as:
options: Partitions
Rules
Scenarios
Tables

mcqs.question: Syntax testing prepares test cases to exercise:
options: All the paths of the program
The rules governing the format of data in a system, e.g. a postal code or a telephone number
The state transitions of the system
The complex business logic of the system

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a demerit of black box testing?
options: The tester must know the implementation and programming languages
It may leave many program paths untested
Tests are done from the developer's point of view
The tester and developer cannot work independently

mcqs.question: Quality planning activities should be carried out:
options: After the regular QA activities
Before carrying out the regular QA activities
Only during the testing phase
Only at project closure

mcqs.question: Setting quality goals involves:
options: Selecting the test tools for the project
Identifying quality views and attributes meaningful to target customers and users, selecting direct quality measures, and quantifying these measures
Writing the glossary of the SQA plan
Scheduling the software reviews

mcqs.question: "The ability of a system to remain operational over time" is the definition of:
options: Availability
Reliability
Scalability
Testability

mcqs.question: Availability defines:
options: The proportion of time that the system is functional and working
The ability of the system to handle increases in load
The degree of ease with which the system can undergo changes
How easy it is to create test criteria for the system

mcqs.question: Scalability is the ability of a system to:
options: Prevent disclosure or loss of information
Be reused in other applications and scenarios
Handle increases in load without impact on the performance of the system
Provide information helpful for identifying and resolving issues

mcqs.question: The SQA Plan structure, containing sections such as Purpose, Reference Documents, Management, Documentation, Standards, Software Reviews and Test, is defined in which standard?
options: ISO 8402
ISO 9126
IEEE 829

mcqs.question: Which section of the SQA Plan (IEEE 730) describes the practices and procedures to be followed for reporting, tracking, and resolving problems?
options: Test
Media control
Problem reporting and corrective action
Supplier control

mcqs.question: Testability is:
options: The responsiveness of a system to execute an action within a given time interval
The ability of different systems to communicate and exchange information with each other
A measure of how easy it is to create test criteria for the system and its components, and to execute these tests to determine if the criteria are met
The capability of a system to prevent malicious or accidental actions

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: Gray box testing is a combination of:
options: Unit testing and system testing
White box testing and black box testing
Static testing and dynamic testing
Manual testing and automated testing

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: In gray box testing, the tester:
options: Has complete knowledge of the internal structure of the system
Is unaware of the internal structure of the system
Partially knows the internal structure and algorithms of the system
Knows only the outputs of the system

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: Regression testing is:
options: Preparing the status report of the project
Re-running of the test cases if new changes are made
Using a subset of all possible combinations of inputs
Testing only the newly added functionality

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: Orthogonal array testing is used as:
options: The complete set of all input combinations
A status reporting technique
A subset of all possible combinations
A code coverage measurement technique

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: White box testing is also known as:
options: Specification based testing
Structural or glass box testing
Acceptance testing
Behavioural testing

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: White box testing is typically undertaken:
options: At the system test phase by the users
At the component and component integration test phases by development teams
At the requirements phase by analysts
At the acceptance phase by customers

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: Statement coverage is calculated as:
options: Number of decisions executed / total number of decisions x 100
Number of statements executed / total number of statements in the source code x 100
Number of paths executed / total number of paths x 100
Number of functions executed / total number of functions x 100

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: A program contains 7 statements in total. A test set executes 5 of these statements. The statement coverage is:

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: Decision coverage (branch coverage) aims to ensure that:
options: Every statement in the code is executed at least once
Each possible branch from each decision point is executed at least once, i.e. every decision is taken each way, true and false
Every path through the program is executed
Every function is called at least once

mcqs.topic: Gray Box and White Box Testing
mcqs.question: The main drawback of statement testing is that:
options: It is too expensive to perform
It cannot test the false condition of a decision
It requires no knowledge of the code
It can only be applied at the system level

mcqs.question: An organization's software process assets include:
options: Only the source code of projects
Standard processes, SDLCs, methodologies and tools, standards, tailoring guidelines and a library of best practices
Only the project schedules
Only the test reports

mcqs.question: Proper process management requires an organization to:
options: Use exactly the same process for every project without any change
Define a standard process, ensure that each project uses an appropriate version of it, and use results to improve the standard process
Avoid taking measurements of the process
Allow every team to invent its own process

mcqs.question: "You cannot improve something if you cannot measure it" is the basis of:
options: Defect prevention
Standard process measurements
Technology innovation
Process change management

mcqs.question: Defect prevention is concerned with:
options: Detecting defects after the product is released
Identifying and eliminating the sources of defects that are inherent in the software process, or of defects that occur repeatedly
Measuring the code coverage of tests
Writing test cases for new functionality

mcqs.question: At the organizational level, defect sources for defect prevention can be identified from:
options: Only the complaints of customers
Only the code reviews of projects
Project wind-up reports, organizational metrics analysis, and audit and assessment reports
Only the test reports of the current project

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a source of input for process change?
options: Marketing and sales reports
Reports from audits and assessments, lessons learnt, change proposals from staff, and process and product measurement data
Competitor analysis reports
Customer purchase data

mcqs.question: Technology innovation (technology change) in an organization helps to:
options: Increase the number of defects
Achieve quality standards resulting in a decrease in defects, reduced process cycle times and increased process effectiveness
Remove the need for a standard software process
Eliminate the need for process measurements
